criteria.browser_entry_hook: Spare the guard file entirely; instead the paired bundle entry point subscribes to htmx:config:request when it detects the generation slot on the page. Regeneration stays out of the change, though header stamping for htmx then belongs to browser startup rather than to the guard that owns every other htmx rule.
criteria.exempt_form: Decline an htmx channel and decline form enforcement together. Nothing about form posting changes under rollout or rollback, which is the smallest possible diff, but the handshake then guards JSON only and stale forms act unchallenged.
criteria.guard_injection: Give the auto-installing htmx guard one more duty: on htmx:config:request, read the live page data-can-generation slot and write it into detail.ctx.request.headers. The same module that already polices htmx targets and swaps would authenticate htmx traffic, in exchange for a guardgen refresh and six pin edits.

htmx_channel.instructions: How should htmx-issued actions obtain the generation header?

criteria.new_identity: Add a bespoke mismatch member to the catalogue failure vocabulary with checker and emitter support, obliging every action declaration to list it and every consumer to match it. Callers see an unmistakable dedicated case, while the change ripples through the catalogue plus all bounds and handlers.
criteria.phase_value: Fold the refusal into the admitted transport failure by having the fetch outcome generation_mismatch lower to http::transport_failed with phase generation. Only runtime code moves, exactly as E04 moved when it added timeout and cancelled phases with the catalogue frozen.

lowering.instructions: Which declared failure should a cross-generation refusal surface as?

criteria.always_pin_uniform: Have each server pin its own manifest buildID and demand a matching header at each action mount, document mounts included. Curl checks, test clients, and companion traffic all need the new header, and document reads by plain navigation turn into refusals.
criteria.paired_pin_json_only: Confine both the pin and the refusal to JSON traffic on paired servers. The htmx surface is never touched, keeping form behavior frozen, while forms issued from outdated pages execute against new servers as if nothing changed.
criteria.paired_pin_selective: Establish the pin solely on paired servers whose manifests read cleanly, preserving unpaired behavior untouched. JSON and form mounts compare the header to the pin; document mounts sit out because navigation cannot emit the header, already delivers the newest document, and has zero mounted programs today.

scope.instructions: How broadly should generation pinning and mismatch refusal reach?

state.client: Can-side JSON actions execute inside fetchJsonAction above native fetch and land in one ActionFetchResult variant: ok, transport, aborted, timeout, codec, or unexpected_status. createJsonActionFetch converts those variants into the six failure identities each action declares, among them http::transport_failed whose phase is a str. Since grid_conflict answers 409 as ordinary domain behavior, the mismatch detector must fire exclusively for the exact mismatch payload and must leave domain 409 traffic on its existing path. The E04 effort previously extended runtime phases with timeout and cancelled and never edited the catalogue.
state.fixed: These points are settled and excluded from judgment: the mismatch reply is status 409 with {schemaVersion 1, kind can.generation-mismatch, serverGeneration holding 64 hex}; pairDocument embeds data-can-generation in the paired script element it splices; the wire header reads can-generation; post-rollback pages refuse identically to rollout pages; asset routes bypass the comparison; a refused action is abandoned rather than retried while the user gets an explicit blocking refresh message instead of an automatic reload. Zero external users means no backwards-compatibility claim constrains the choice.
state.handshake: A paired shipment joins one server generation, named by the 64-hex buildID inside its manifest, to one browser build. HTML served from that generation discloses its identity with a data-can-generation slot on the paired script tag, and action calls made by living page logic return the slot in a can-generation header. Absent, misshapen, or merely non-identical values draw the typed 409 mismatch before action code starts, after which the program shows a blocking refresh notice.
state.htmx: Forms travel via the vendored pinned htmx 4.0.0, whose htmx:config:request event exposes detail.ctx.request.headers for mutation ahead of dispatch. The owned guard script bootstraps itself onto all htmx pages, rules on targets, responses, and swaps, depends on zero imports, and rebuilds with guardgen plus six integrity pin revisions. Raw navigation events like reloads or address entries support no custom headers by browser design, yet every one of them fetches the latest document from whoever serves now.
state.server: Action authors expose JSON, form, and document endpoints using mount, mountForm, and mountDocument from createActionRoutes against a shared router, where dispatch matches requests via the compiled capture table. The root URL supplied to createAssets denotes the generation folder under service, so manifest.json and the buildID live right there. Pairless servers keep fielding curl invocations, test drivers, and similar headerless action users, and presently no codebase mounts any document action.
